problems.title: Scorer can replace the labeled question with a system instruction
claim: The evaluator scores against messages[0] instead of selecting the user question by role. Released predictions include a system message before the question.
analysis: Consider two items with identical system instruction, reference letter A and model response happy. In one user question A means happy; in the other A means sad. Correct judgments differ, but selecting only the system message makes both judge prompts identical and omits both option lists. No deterministic or stochastic judge can recover the missing distinction from identical inputs. A directly inspected released VidEmo emotion record uses this system-first schema.
result: The supplied scorer and raw records have an information-losing interface mismatch. A private user-first cleaning stage might have been used historically; the published score impact is not established.
repair: Select and validate the actual user message, preserve task instructions/options and required dialogue context, and remove only known video placeholders.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a current release evaluation-interface defect, with original scoring-input provenance and numeric table changes unresolved.

problems.title: Scoring failures change denominators inconsistently
problems.source_location: Appendix D.3; eval/eval_results.py, eval_single and result_evaluate, lines 215–269
claim: Exhausted judge requests can be absent from the stored results. Numeric scores average stored responses, while yes/no accuracy divides by all submitted records.
analysis: For two submitted items with only one successful score of \(100\), the numeric branch reports \(100\), while one successful yes gives accuracy \(50\). The missing numeric value could be anywhere in \([0,100]\), so the full mean is only identified within \([50,100]\). In general, if N are expected, m are scored and observed sum is A, the full mean lies in \([A/N,(A+100(N-m))/N]\).
result: The current metrics use different failure semantics and may summarize different populations. No actual original judge-failure rate or direction of benchmark bias is established; complete successful scoring avoids this problem.
repair: Keep one indexed status for every expected record, validate accepted scores, and report complete means or an explicit failure policy. Conditional means and worst-case missing-score bounds should be labeled separately.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a conditional aggregation-contract defect; observed benchmark bias or ranking changes are not demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.
